title: Anthropic AI & Lean 4 Prove the Critical Dying Percolation Conjecture (θ(p_c) = 0)
whyItMatters: Settles probability theory’s 66-year-old 'holy grail'—proving no infinite cluster survives at the critical percolation threshold θ(p_c) = 0 in every dimension d ≥ 3, verified in Lean 4 and streamlined by human experts.
summary: On August 26, 2026, a dangling commit (795efb8) by Justin Leder in Anthropic’s formal-math GitHub repository surfaced a Lean 4 proof of Kozma and Nitzan’s (2024) correlation inequality—immediately settling the 66-year-old dying percolation conjecture (θ(p_c) = 0 on ℤ^d in all dimensions, including the physically central 3D case). Discovered by mathematicians on X just days before Fields Medalist Hugo Duminil-Copin predicted AI would crack it first, the proof was rapidly checked, explained by Ahmed Bou-Rabee (extending it to site percolation), condensed to 9 human-readable pages by Arthur Blanc-Renaudie, and generalized to FK-percolation (arXiv:2610.26419).
technicalHighlights: Resolves θ(p_c) = 0 on ℤ^d for all intermediate dimensions d ≥ 3 (including d = 3), closing the main long-standing open problem in percolation theory since Harris (1960).
Proves Kozma–Nitzan’s (2024) general finite weighted-graph correlation inequality in Lean 4—a conjecture many specialists had suspected might have a counterexample.
Independently verified, streamlined into a 9-page human proof by Arthur Blanc-Renaudie, and generalized to site percolation and random-cluster (FK) models (arXiv:2610.26419).
caveats: Originally surfaced via an unannounced GitHub commit rather than a traditional paper; journal publication of the streamlined human expositions and FK-percolation generalizations is still working through peer review.

scoreRationale.foundational: Solves what Fields Medalist Hugo Duminil-Copin and Gil Kalai called the most famous open conjecture in percolation theory (open since 1960).
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly impacts statistical mechanics, phase-transition theory, and random-cluster (FK) models, immediately sparking new generalizations.
scoreRationale.verification: Gold-standard dual verification: complete Lean 4 formalization plus concise 9-page human proofs and independent arXiv extensions.
scoreRationale.velocity: Cracked a 66-year-old 'holy grail' of probability theory autonomously and proved an inequality experts thought might be false.
